Documentation → FortiWeb: Policies & Protection → Fleet Objects

Fleet Objects

One table of every server policy, web protection profile or server pool across all your FortiWeb appliances, with filters, an any-field search and CSV export.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsprotection.view
📍 WhereFortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM → Operations → Fleet Objects (URL /fleet-objects)

What is it?#

Fleet Objects answers "where is this configured?" across the whole fleet. It puts the server policies, web protection profiles or server pools of every FortiWeb you can see into one table, with a Device column, filter drop-downs and CSV export. A fourth mode searches any value in any field of those objects.

What does it do?#

The page has four modes, selected with the buttons at the top:

Mode Columns (after Device) Filter drop-downs
Server Policy Name, Deployment mode, Virtual server, Server pool, Web Protection Profile, Status Mode, Status, WPP
Web Protection Profile Name, Kind, Signature rule, IP intelligence, File upload, Webshell Kind, IP intel, Signature rule
Server Pool Name, Type, Protocol Type, Protocol
Search (any field) Device, Section, Type, Object, Field, Value —
  • In the three typed modes, the drop-downs list the distinct values found and filter on an exact match; the text box filters rows whose visible columns contain the text. The counter reads N shown / M total.
  • Web Protection Profile mode lists both inline and offline protection profiles; Kind tells them apart.
  • Search (any field) returns one row per matching field: the search text is matched, case-insensitively, against both field names and values of every server policy, web protection profile and server pool. Results are capped at 1,000 rows. The counter reads N match(es).
  • Export CSV downloads exactly the current view as fleet_objects_<mode>.csv.

The page only reads. It never contacts an appliance: rows come from SATOM's local copy of each device's configuration.

Requirements#

  • Appliances registered in SATOM whose configuration has been synchronised at least once. A device with no local copy contributes no rows.

Permissions#

Opening Fleet Objects needs protection.view; without it the sidebar entry is hidden and the page answers 403 Forbidden. The rows are limited to the appliances you may see: the current ADOM's devices (all devices in the Global ADOM), excluding devices in maintenance mode unless you hold appliances.view_maintenance.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: Fleet Objects now needs protection.view; before, any signed-in user could open it.

How to use#

List objects across devices#

  1. Open Operations → Fleet Objects in the FortiWeb or FortiADC ADOM. (Since 2026-10-14 the Global ADOM's menu no longer lists it; /fleet-objects still opens there from a bookmark and shows every device.)
  2. Click a mode, for example Server Policy.
  3. Pick a value in a drop-down (for example Mode: (any) → server-pool). The page reloads with the filter applied.
  4. Optionally type text in filter rows… and click Apply.

Find a value anywhere#

  1. Click Search (any field).
  2. Type the value in search any field across the fleet…, for example an IP address or a profile name, and click Search.
  3. Each row shows the device, the object type, the object name, the field and its value.

Export#

Click Export CSV. The file contains the same columns and rows as the current view, including the active filters and text.

Configuration#

Control Description Required Example
Mode Server Policy, Web Protection Profile, Server Pool or Search (any field). Yes (defaults to Server Policy) Server Pool
Filter drop-downs Exact-match filter on one column; (any) clears it. No Protocol: HTTP
Text box Typed modes: substring filter over the visible columns. Search mode: the query. Required in Search mode 192.0.2.10

Example#

🧪Example — Which policies still use the old profile?

  1. Open Fleet Objects → Server Policy.
  2. In WPP: (any) pick wpp-legacy.
  3. The table lists every policy on every device bound to wpp-legacy, e.g. fweb-01 · spol-shop and fweb-02 · spol-api.
  4. Click Export CSV to share the list.

Result#

Nothing is changed and nothing is written to the audit log; the page and the CSV are views of SATOM's local configuration copy.

Troubleshooting#

"No objects found"#

Possible causes - No appliance has a local configuration copy yet, or the filters exclude every row.

Solution 1. Reset the filters to (any) and clear the text box. 2. Refresh the device's configuration — for example with the refresh button in Server Objects or an Automation device sync.

Verification - The counter shows a non-zero total.

"Type a term to search"#

Search mode has no default query; type a value and click Search.

"No matches for """#

No field name or value of any server policy, web protection profile or server pool contains the text. Search mode does not cover other object types; use Search for a wider search.

A device you expected is missing#

Possible causes - The device belongs to another ADOM, is in maintenance mode, or has never been synchronised.

Solution 1. Switch to the Global ADOM, or synchronise the device.

The data looks out of date#

The table reflects the last synchronisation of each device, not the live configuration. Refresh the device, then reload the page.

Advanced#

Advanced Data source

Rows are read from the local configuration store: server policies, server pools, and inline plus offline web protection profiles. Each column takes the first non-empty value among a list of candidate field names, so differences in field naming between firmware versions render as the same column; a missing field renders as —. List values are joined with commas and boolean values render as enable / disable.
